newsitem.title: CYPRUS: SOCCER-CYPRUS F.A. MEET ON MATCH-FIXING CLAIMS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CYPRUS F.A. MEET ON MATCH-FIXING CLAIMS.

text.p: The Cyprus F.A. is due to meet later on Monday to seek police aid in their probe into allegations of match fixing in a World Cup qualifier against Bulgaria on December 14.
Members of the federation are due to ask for police intervention to investigate claims players in the national team placed heavy bets on losing to Bulgaria, a key member said on Monday.

The allegations, reported extensively by the local media, do not mention any specific player, but football authorities admit that the sums bet on the match -- up to 10 times the normal -- are enough to arouse suspicion.
Cyprus lost 3-1 to Bulgaria in Limassol.

"What aroused our suspicions was that usually around 3,000 pounds ($6,400) is placed on such games and this time 30,000 pounds was placed in bets," Cyprus F.A. vice chairman Costas Koutsokoumnis told a parliamentary inquiry.
The F.A. official said bookmakers even rejected bets because the sums placed made them suspicious.
But Koutsokoumnis said he thought the possibility of drawing a link between the bets and the players was unlikely.
"I can only say the performance of some players (in the qualifying match) was not as it normally is in other games," he said.
"But this could easily be countered with an excuse like they had the flu or were not feeling well."
The F.A. is pushing for a ban on all betting involving national teams and local teams, he said.
